subject.title: fix(codex): fail-closed on unknown item statuses and warn on dropped notifications

question: Should OpenClaw treat every explicit unknown Codex item status as failed by default, and which open candidate should own the canonical fix after correlation logging is moved to the real router drop boundary?
rationale: Direct Codex inspection shows the patch does not alter current known statuses, but fail-closed handling defines future upgrade behavior and multiple open PRs implement different correlation policies, so automation cannot safely select the permanent contract.

options.title: Accept fail-closed and repair this PR
options.body: Keep explicit unknown statuses as failed, move stale-turn warnings to the router, add routed proof, and use this PR as the canonical candidate.

options.title: Prefer warn-only compatibility
options.body: Warn on unknown explicit statuses without changing their projected success behavior until a stricter compatibility policy is separately approved.

options.title: Choose another candidate
options.body: Select https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99287 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102396 as canonical and close the other candidates only after the chosen path is demonstrably viable.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed and repair this PR
recommendation.body: Keep explicit unknown statuses as failed, move stale-turn warnings to the router, add routed proof, and use this PR as the canonical candidate.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant harness architecture and hardening history most strongly trace to this owner.
